longTitle.officialTitle: To enhance cooperation between the Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General to combat unfair and deceptive practices, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “FTC Collaboration Act of 2021”.

section.heading: UNFAIR AND DECEPTIVE PRACTICES COOPERATION STUDY.

paragraph.heading: Study required.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Federal Trade Commission shall conduct a study on facilitating and refining existing efforts with State Attorneys General to prevent, publicize, and penalize frauds and scams being perpetrated on individuals in the United States.

paragraph.heading: Requirements of study.—
paragraph.chapeau: In conducting the study, the Commission shall examine the following:

subparagraph.content: The roles and responsibilities of the Commission and State Attorneys General that best advance collaboration and consumer protection.
The policies, procedures, and mechanisms that facilitate cooperation and communications across the Commission.
How resources should be dedicated to best advance such collaboration and consumer protection.
The accountability mechanisms that should be implemented to promote collaboration and consumer protection.

paragraph.heading: Consultation and public comment.—
paragraph.chapeau: In producing the study required in paragraph (1), the Commission shall—

clause.content: the National Association of State Attorneys General;
public interest organizations dedicated to consumer protection;
any other Federal or State agency that the Federal Trade Commission considers necessary; and

subparagraph.content: provide opportunity for public comment and advice relevant to the production of the study.

subsection.heading: Report to Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 6 months after the completion of the study required pursuant to subsection (a), the Commission shall submit to the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate, and make publicly available on the website of the Commission, a report that contains the following:

paragraph.content: Recommended best practices to enhance collaboration efforts between the Commission and State Attorneys General with respect to preventing, publicizing, and penalizing fraud and scams.
Quantifiable metrics by which enhanced collaboration can be measured.
Legislative recommendations, if any, to enhance collaboration efforts between the Commission and State Attorneys General to prevent, publicize, and penalize fraud and scams.

subsection.heading: Commission Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “Commission” means the Federal Trade Commission.
